analysis: Documentation-only changes. docs/architecture/inference.md head 1235-1821 was examined. In this unit the only changed line is 1780, which adds the code-map reference to AdmissionRateEstimators.swift (DeadlineAdmissionFixes, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate). The other changed ranges (632-638 rate-freshness anchoring; 882-918 estimator corrections gated by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES) are visible only via the partial patch excerpt and belong to other units. docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md lines 3 and 15-22 change the date and state that the estimator corrections need no timing-catalog entry and that calibratedPathProven still separates two conversions. These texts describe deadline/admission estimators: availability and scheduling heuristics with an operator rollback switch. They do not touch the provider wire/encryption (TB-002, T-008), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), prefix-cache identity, TTL or HMAC naming (T-041/SEC-035), or authorization. The sampler and cache-identity statements at 1257-1259 and the context-limit checks at 1682-1685 appear unchanged. Integration question: the referenced Swift sources (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate) were not supplied. Integration should verify that estimator changes cannot be driven by consumer-controlled inputs to cause unbounded admission or bypass the physical KV and memory gates (T-010/T-029-style availability). It should also confirm that the rate-freshness change does not let stale evidence appear fresh in capacity reports sent to the coordinator. No security regression is evident from the docs alone.
